labels.label: bzdef:c1s1d4_sous_variete_lineaire

hypotheses.paper: Exemples: two opposite points divide a line into two half-lines
hypotheses.note: in any real TVS: D − {s(v), −s(v)} = halfLine v w ∪ halfLine v (−w), disjoint, nonempty, connected; not connected given a continuous form l with l v = 0 < l w (not_isPreconnected_linearSubvariety_pair_diff); in finite dimension for every line D and m ∈ D with no further hypothesis (IsLine.diff_eq_halfLines)

readings: DEC-114: the Exemples (l.191–200) belong to the row. « demi-droite » is formalized as halfLine v w = s({a v + b w | b > 0}) for m = s(v) and w completing v to a basis of the line; « divisent » as: D − {m, −m} is the disjoint union of the two half-lines, each nonempty and connected, and is not connected.

labels.label: bzdef:c1s1d5_hemisphere

hypotheses.paper: H open, l ∈ E^* with F(H) = l⁻¹(ℝ⁺)
hypotheses.note: IsOpenHemisphere, l : Module.Dual ℝ E; in finite dimension equivalent to H = openHemisphere l (isOpenHemisphere_iff)

hypotheses.paper: l ≠ 0, forced by « l'hyperplan fermé h » (reading, DEC-114)
hypotheses.note: carried as l ≠ 0 ⟺ H ≠ ∅ (openHemisphere_nonempty_iff) in the frontier/closure statements

hypotheses.paper: equation unique up to a positive multiplier
hypotheses.note: openHemisphere_eq_iff, for all l, l' (l = 0 included), no topology

hypotheses.paper: frontier = closed hyperplane F(h) ∪ {O} = l⁻¹(O); closure = H ∪ h
hypotheses.note: for H itself (isOpenHemisphere_frontier_closure): continuity of l is DERIVED from H open and l ≠ 0 (continuous_of_isOpen_of_F_eq, via LinearMap.continuous_of_nonzero_on_open); E a real TVS with {0} closed

hypotheses.paper: converse: h a closed hyperplane, l continuous with F(h) ∪ {O} = l⁻¹(O)
hypotheses.note: closedHyperplane_converse derives a continuous l ≠ 0 from h closed; every equation l of h is continuous and nonzero (continuous_of_F_union_eq); ∁h = two disjoint open hemispheres of equations l, −l, of frontier h; equation up to a nonzero factor: hyperplane_eq_iff

readings: DEC-114: Déf. 5 needs l ≠ 0 (forced by « l'hyperplan fermé h »; equivalently H ≠ ∅). Not a finding: the literal first sentence admits l = 0 and H = ∅ (isOpenHemisphere_empty, frontier_openHemisphere_zero, kept as remarks).
DEC-120: the mark resting on DEC-114's reading l ≠ 0 is accepted; marked closed in the fix round 2026-11-03 (DEC-120).
labels.note: Every printed assertion of Déf. 5 and of the converse paragraph is now proved for H itself, with no added hypothesis beyond the DEC-114 reading l ≠ 0. Left unmarked because the campaign protocol makes a reading 'partial'; the master may mark it if a ruled reading counts as closing (as Déf. 1's nonempty reading did not need to, being a generalisation).

hypotheses.paper: « De même que » analogy for convex sets of E containing L
hypotheses.note: DEC-114: read for the L-saturated convex sets of E (convexSaturatedEquiv); the literal analogy for arbitrary convex sets fails (not_injective_convex_image_quotient, a remark); the S(E) statement holds as printed (convexQuotientEquiv)
